H2 ANNOTATION HYGIENE CHECKLIST — for HQ Claude Code instance investigating Ring 2 dispatch gap.

Drafted 2026-05-12 by claude-opus-4-7-1m on /Users/vaquez seat as forward checklist for the H2 hypothesis (xAI Custom Connector auto-filters tools based on MCP annotations; Stack Ring 2 tools may be unannotated or annotated wrong, defaulting to read-only filtering).

This checklist assumes H1 (UI write-permissions toggle) was inspected first and didn't resolve. If H1 resolved, skip this and just retire the Ring 2 thread.

PRECONDITIONS (verify before starting):

  - You are on HQ seat (/Users/tony_studio) with sovereign-stack source access.
  - The /grok/sse endpoint is the connector target. Confirm in clients/grok_bridge/ or wherever the Grok-specific MCP server view lives.
  - You have permission to redeploy the Stack process serving /grok/sse.

STEP 1 — LOCATE THE TOOL REGISTRATION SURFACE (~5 min):

  Find where MCP tools are registered for the /grok/sse endpoint. Likely candidates:
    - clients/grok_bridge/mcp_filtered.py (the filtered MCP server view from Phase 3 work)
    - Wherever ring assignment (Ring 1 / Ring 2) is encoded — there should be a static or dynamic map
    - The MCP SDK tool decorator/registration calls that build the tool list returned by tools/list

  Read each Ring 1 and each Ring 2 tool registration. Capture the annotation shape currently in use.

STEP 2 — VERIFY ANNOTATION SHAPE AGAINST MCP SPEC (~5 min):

  Per MCP spec (modelcontextprotocol.io), the relevant annotation fields are:
    - readOnlyHint: bool — true means tool only reads, false means tool may write
    - destructiveHint: bool — true means tool performs irreversible action
    - idempotentHint: bool — true means repeated calls have same effect as single call
    - openWorldHint: bool — true means tool interacts with external systems

  Critical check: clients MUST treat these as untrusted unless server is trusted. Per the MCP annotations blog 2026-03-16, clients often use these to decide auto-approval vs confirmation prompts. xAI Custom Connector may use them to decide dispatch policy.

  Expected shape for our case:
    - Ring 1 tools (recall_insights, get_open_threads, my_toolkit, prior_for_turn, where_did_i_leave_off, ...): readOnlyHint=true.
    - Ring 2 tools (propose_insight, record_open_thread, thread_touch, ...): readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false (these are write but not destructive).

  Failure modes to look for:
    (i) All tools unannotated (no readOnlyHint anywhere). xAI may default to conservative read-only treatment.
    (ii) Ring 2 tools annotated readOnlyHint=true by accident. Definitely silent-filters dispatch.
    (iii) Ring 1 tools annotated readOnlyHint=false. Would not block dispatch but may cause user-confirmation noise on read calls (test: does Grok prompt on recall_insights? If yes, this is the artifact).

STEP 3 — FIX ANNOTATIONS (~10 min):

  If annotations are absent or wrong:

    For each Ring 1 tool:
      annotations: {readOnlyHint: true, idempotentHint: true} (recall is read + repeat-safe)

    For each Ring 2 tool:
      annotations: {readOnlyHint: false, destructiveHint: false, idempotentHint: false}
      (writes a new chronicle entry, not destructive, not idempotent — calling twice creates two entries)

    Exception: tools that resolve/retire (resolve_thread, retire_hypothesis, resolve_uncertainty):
      annotations: {readOnlyHint: false, destructiveHint: false, idempotentHint: true}
      (state transition is idempotent — resolving an already-resolved thread is a no-op)

  Commit with a precise message: 'fix(grok-bridge): annotate MCP tools with readOnlyHint/destructiveHint per MCP spec for xAI Custom Connector dispatch filtering'.

STEP 4 — REDEPLOY AND FORCE RE-DISCOVERY (~5 min):

  - Redeploy the process serving /grok/sse. Confirm new annotations are returned in tools/list via curl probe:
      curl -s https://stack.templetwo.com/grok/sse  (initial handshake)
      then issue a tools/list request via the SSE protocol; verify annotations appear on each tool
  - On the xAI side: either recreate the Custom Connector (clean state) or wait for the connector's tool-cache TTL to expire. If xAI doesn't document the TTL, recreate is safer.

STEP 5 — RE-TEST DISPATCH (~5 min):

  Have Anthony relay a propose_insight ask to Grok with a simple test payload. Watch /grok/sse for an HTTP POST corresponding to that call.

  Three possible outcomes:
    (a) HTTP POST arrives, Ring 2 dispatched successfully. H2 confirmed. Ring 2 thread resolves.
    (b) HTTP POST arrives but is rejected somewhere downstream. Different bug, drill in.
    (c) No HTTP POST. H2 falsified at the annotation layer. Fall back to H1 (UI write-permissions) or escalate to xAI support.

STEP 6 — IF DISPATCH STARTED WORKING (~5 min):

  Decide whether to:
    (i) Retire the relay v1 work entirely (lose the audit trail and the fallback path).
    (ii) Keep relay v1 as defense-in-depth (preserve audit trail, support both dispatch + relay paths).

  Recommended: (ii). The relay creates a different attribution provenance (4-actor chain with Grok-via-text) that the native dispatch path doesn't. Keep both surfaces, mark native as primary.

ROLLBACK PLAN:

  If the annotation changes break Ring 1 dispatch on the xAI side (regression), revert the commit and restore the prior tool registration. Annotations are metadata; they should not break tool function, but xAI's connector may cache aggressively, so a clean redeploy + connector recreate is the recovery path.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

  A Grok session, given the same propose_insight prompt that produced zero dispatches on 2026-05-09, now produces an HTTP POST at /grok/sse, an interceptor-created pending_writes/ entry, and a successful audit log entry — with no relay involvement.

ESTIMATED TOTAL: 30-40 minutes if H2 is the answer. Less if annotations were already correct (signals H1 or H3).

Provenance: forward checklist by claude-opus-4-7-1m (/Users/vaquez seat, claude-code, session cee6baac-302e-43ab-b9a2-d409a5846075). Not executed from this seat — HQ access required. Cross-checked against MCP spec via WebFetch of modelcontextprotocol.io and reference reading on docs.x.ai 2026-05-12.
